Rashi on Bekhorot 38b:10:1.english: Pale spots - It is an illness in which there are white drops in the eye.

Rashi on Bekhorot 38b:10:2.english: That are constant - [This] refers to both of them — to the pale spots and to the tears.

Rashi on Bekhorot 38b:10:3.hebrew: בודקין ג"פ בתוך שמונים יום - ואם לא בדקוהו, אע"פ שמום נמצא שם ביום שמונים — לא הוי מום, דשמא בינתים הלך לו וחזר, שכן דרכו:
Rashi on Bekhorot 38b:10:3.english: One examines [it] three times within eighty days - And if they did not examine it, even though a blemish is found there on the eightieth day, it is not [considered a permanent] blemish, for perhaps in the interim it went away and returned, as such is its nature.

Rashi on Bekhorot 38b:11:1.english: Water - That its eyes drip water.

Rashi on Bekhorot 38b:11:2.hebrew: אלו הם המים הקבועין - כלומר, במאי ידעינן אי קבועין הן, אי עוברים:
Rashi on Bekhorot 38b:11:2.english: These are the permanent tears - That is to say, how do we know whether they are permanent or temporary.

Rashi on Bekhorot 38b:1:2.hebrew: תורא ברא דעינא - שורה חיצונה של עין, היינו בת עין המכסה את העין:
Rashi on Bekhorot 38b:1:2.english: The outer line of the eye - The outer row of the eye; that is, the eyelid [lit., daughter of the eye], which covers the eye.

Rashi on Bekhorot 38b:1:3.hebrew: דק משוקע - דק המשקע את העין, הרי זה מום:
Rashi on Bekhorot 38b:1:3.english: A sunken cataract - A cataract that depresses the eye — behold, this is a blemish.

Rashi on Bekhorot 38b:2:1.hebrew: הא בשחור הא בלבן - השתא קס"ד דמוקים חדא בשחור של עין, וחדא בלבן של עין:
Rashi on Bekhorot 38b:2:1.english: This [is] in the black, that [is] in the white - Now it enters your mind that [the Gemara] establishes one in the black of the eye, and one in the white of the eye.

Rashi on Bekhorot 38b:3:1.hebrew: וסימניך ברקא - מייל"א, דהוי לבן וצף והוי מום. הכא נמי, סימן זה יהא לך בדוק — דלבן וצף הוי מום:
Rashi on Bekhorot 38b:3:1.english: And your mnemonic is barka - [It refers to] maille [a cataract], which is white and floating, and is a blemish. Here too, let this sign be for you regarding a cataract [dok]: that white and floating is a blemish.

Rashi on Bekhorot 38b:3:2.hebrew: ברקא - כגון השוכר את החמור והבריקה (ב"מ דף עח.):
Rashi on Bekhorot 38b:3:2.english: Barka - Such as: “One who rents a donkey and it developed a cataract [vehivrika]” (Bava Metzia 78a).

Rashi on Bekhorot 38b:5:1.english: A certain elder - He was a priest.

Rashi on Bekhorot 38b:5:2.english: I did not pass before him - For he was the greatest of the generation.

Rashi on Bekhorot 38b:5:3.hebrew: חלזון זה - בכור היה לו לאותו זקן, והיה לו חלזון בעינים:
Rashi on Bekhorot 38b:5:3.english: This snail - That elder had a firstborn [animal], and it had a snail[-like growth] in [its] eyes.

Rashi on Bekhorot 38b:7:1.english: That [he] is ruling a halakha - A new halakha that we did not hear from another.

Rashi on Bekhorot 38b:7:2.english: Before the incident - Before a practical case of the halakha came into his hands.

Rashi on Bekhorot 38b:7:3.english: One listens to him - And one acts in practice [in accordance with his ruling].

Rashi on Bekhorot 38b:7:4.hebrew: אין שומעין לו - דבשביל המעשה אומרה. והכא, מאן ציית ליה במאי דאמר דמום קבוע הוא:
Rashi on Bekhorot 38b:7:4.english: One does not listen to him - For he states it on account of the incident. And here, who would listen to him regarding what he said, that it is a permanent blemish?

Rashi on Bekhorot 38b:8:1.hebrew: מתניתין - דקתני אין מום בלבן, רבי יוסי היא:
Rashi on Bekhorot 38b:8:1.english: The mishna - Which teaches [that] there is no blemish in the white [of the eye], is [according to] Rabbi Yosei:

Rashi on Bekhorot 38b:9:1.hebrew: יצא מחלב עינימו - יצא רשע לתרבות רעה מרוב שומן שבעינו, ושומן העין בלבן הוא:
Rashi on Bekhorot 38b:9:1.english: “Their eyes stand forth from fatness” - A wicked person turned to corrupt ways from the abundance of fat in his eye; and the fat of the eye is in the white [part].

Rashi on Bekhorot 38b:9:2.hebrew: דבר המבלבל - שפוסק הסירא ומערב השחור והלבן; כל היכי דעבר, הוי מבלבל:
Rashi on Bekhorot 38b:9:2.english: A substance that mixes - For it cuts through the ring and mixes the black and the white; whichever way it crosses, it is mixing.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 38b:3:1.hebrew: וסימניך ברקא - משמע דהוי מום קבוע. ותימה, דבפ' מי שאחזו (גיטין סט.) יש רפואות לברקא, ובפרק המוציא יין (שבת עח.) נמי אמרי': כוחלין לברקותי! וי"ל, דהתם מיירי בממשמשין ובאין קודם שנקבעו. וכן נמי [צריך] לתרץ אקושיא אחריתי, דהתם בפרק המוציא יין קתני (ג"ז שם): דם כדי לכחול עין אחת, שכך כוחלין (ליחוור) [ליארוד], ובתוספתא (דשבת פ"ט) גרסי' להו, ובתוספתא במכילתין (פ"ד) כתוב יאור במקום חורוור — משמע דהכל אחד, וחורוור הקבוע חשיב לקמן מום; ומיהו איכא למימר דבשבת מיירי באותו שאינו קבוע. ועוד יש לתרץ, דהיכא דאין מתרפא מאליו חשיב מום. והא דקאמר לקמן גבי מים הקבועים דאם עובר כשמאכילין אותו לח ויבש של גשמים לא הוי קבוע — אין זו רפואה ממש, אלא בדיקה ונסיון אם הם קבועים אם לאו; אבל רפואה גמורה יכולה להעביר מום קבוע. תדע, דלקמן (בכורות דף לט:) אמרינן גבי נפגם הזובן: נפגם ולא ניטל, דניטל חוזר לאיתנו יותר, וכשנפגם נמי הוי יכול ליטלו. ומיהו י"ל, דכי נפגם תחלה אין לו תקנה. וקצת יש לדקדק מילפת דכתיבא באורייתא והוי מום כדלקמן (בכורות דף מא.), והיא חזזית המצרית, ובב"ק בפרק מרובה (בבא קמא דף פ:) משמע דיש לה רפואה, כדאמרינן: מתריעין על החיכוך בשבת, ומוקי לה בחזזית המצרית דלח מבחוץ ויבש מבפנים. ומיהו יש לפרש, דהא שמתריעין לאו שתתרפא אלא שלא תוסיף; דמה נפשך אין לה רפואה, דאמרי' לקמן שמלפפת והולכת עד יום המיתה, וכתיב נמי אשר לא תוכל להרפא. ומיהו יש לדקדק מיבלת דכתיבא והויא מום כדלקמן, ותנן בפ' המוצא תפילין (עירובין קג.): חותכין יבלת במקדש, וכן חותכין יבלת בפסח (פסחים סה:) — אלמא יש לה רפואה בחתיכה, וחשיב מום! ואין להעמידה דלית בה עצם, דתלתולי בעלמא הוא כדלקמן. ומיהו יש להעמידה ביבלת שבעין ודלית ביה שער, דאין שוחטין עלה לא במקדש ולא במדינה; ואע"ג דאמרי' בעירובין (שם): לחה ויבשה, יד וכלי — הכל שייך ביבלת שבעין:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 38b:3:1.english: "And your mnemonic is barka" - This implies that it is a permanent blemish. And this is difficult, for in the chapter [entitled] Mi She'aḥazo (Gittin 69a), there are remedies for barka; and in the chapter [entitled] HaMotsi Yayin (Shabbat 78a), we also say: "They paint [the eye] with kohl for barkati"! And one can say that there [in Shabbat and Gittin] it is dealing with [blemishes] that are impending [and advancing], before they have become permanently established. And so too [it is necessary] to answer another difficulty: for there in the chapter [entitled] HaMotsi Yayin, it teaches (there as well): "[The measure of] blood [for carrying on Shabbat is] enough to paint one eye with kohl, for so they paint with kohl for (ḥevar) [yarod]"; and in the Tosefta (of Shabbat, ch. 9) they read them [both]; and in the Tosefta in our tractate (ch. 4), it is written ya'or in place of ḥurvar, which implies that they are all one [and the same]; and permanent ḥurvar is considered a blemish below [44a]! However, one can say that in Shabbat it is dealing with that which is not permanent. And furthermore, one can answer that wherever it does not heal on its own, it is considered a [permanent] blemish. And that which [the Gemara] says below regarding permanent discharges [of the eye], that if it passes when they feed [the animal] moist and dry [grasses] of the rainy season, it is not permanent — this is not an actual remedy, but rather an examination and a test [to determine] whether they are permanent or not; however, a complete remedy can indeed remove a permanent blemish. You should know [that this is so], for below (Bekhorot 39b) we say regarding [the blemish of] "the sheath [of the penis] was notched": [it is a blemish only if it was] notched, but not severed, for if it was severed, it recovers its strength more [and heals]; and when it is notched, he would also be able to sever it [so that it heals, yet it is considered a blemish]! However, one can say that when it was notched initially, it has no remedy. And one can infer somewhat [a question against this] from yalephet [Egyptian lichen], which is written in the Torah and is a blemish as stated below (Bekhorot 41a), and it is [identical to] Egyptian ḥazazit; and in Bava Kamma, in the chapter [entitled] Merubah (Bava Kamma 80b), it implies that there is a remedy for it, as we say: "They sound the alarm for an itch on Shabbat," and [the Gemara] establishes it as referring to Egyptian ḥazazit, where it is moist on the outside and dry on the inside. However, one can explain that this [fact] that they sound the alarm is not so that it should be healed, but rather that it should not spread [further]; for in any event (mah nafshekh) it has no remedy, as we say below that it clings and continues until the day of death, and it is also written: "from which you cannot be healed" (Deuteronomy 28:27). However, one can infer [a proof that curable conditions can be blemishes] from a wart (yabelet), which is written [in the Torah] and is a blemish as stated below; and we learned in a mishnah in the chapter [entitled] HaMotse Tefillin (Eruvin 103a): "They may cut a wart in the Temple," and so too "they may cut a wart on Passover" (Pesachim 65b) — thus, it has a remedy by cutting, and yet it is considered a blemish! And one cannot establish [the mishnah where they cut it] where it has no bone, because [a wart without a bone] is merely dangling [flesh] as stated below. However, one can establish it as referring to a wart in the eye and which has no hair, for which they do not slaughter [the animal as blemished] either in the Temple or in the rest of the land; and even though we say in Eruvin (ibid.): "[a wart that is] moist or dry, [removed by] hand or with an implement," all [of these distinctions] apply to a wart in the eye.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 38b:7:1.hebrew: אם קודם מעשה אמרה שומעין לו - אומר ר"ת דלא אמרי' הכי אלא היכא דצריך לאותה הוראה, כי הכא; וביבמות בפ' הערל (יבמות דף עו.) גבי "חגר חרב כישמעאל", ובפרק נושאין על האנוסה (יבמות צח.) גבי "גר נושא אשת אחיו מאמו", ובריש עשרה יוחסין (קדושין ע:) גבי עובדא דרב יהודה, ד"כל דאמר מבית חשמונאי אתינא עבדא הוא" — שהיה נראה לרב יהודה שאומר כן לפי שהקניטו:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 38b:7:1.english: "If he stated it before the incident, one listens to him" - Rabbeinu Tam says that we only say this where [the scholar] needs that ruling [for himself], as [is the case] here; and in Yevamot, in the chapter [entitled] Ha'arel (Yevamot 76a), regarding [the one who] "girded [his] sword like Ishmael"; and in the chapter [entitled] Nos’in Al Ha'anusa (Yevamot 98a), regarding [the case of] "a convert [who] marries the wife of his maternal brother"; and at the beginning of [the chapter entitled] Asarah Yuḥasin (Kiddushin 70b), regarding the incident involving Rav Yehuda, where [he ruled that] "anyone who says, 'I come from the Hasmonean house,' is a slave" — where it appeared regarding Rav Yehuda that he was saying so because [the man] had provoked him.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 38b:9:1.hebrew: יצא מחלב עינימו - לפי הדרשה, לבן שבעין קורין חלב, כדפי' בקונטרס ששם שומן העין; ורוצה לומר שיצא הרשע לתרבות רעה מרוב שומן שבעין. אבל פשטיה דקרא רוצה לומר שיוצא העין ובולט לחוץ מרוב שומן שבתוכו:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 38b:9:1.english: “Their eyes stand forth from fatness” - According to the homiletical interpretation, the white of the eye is called “fat,” as explained in the Kuntres [Rashi] that the fat of the eye is located there; and it means that the wicked person went out to an evil path [tarbut ra'ah] due to an abundance of fat in the eye. But the plain meaning of the verse means that the eye protrudes and bulges outward from the abundance of fat within it.
